e do not define operation or accessibility requirements. If no application record exists, record that gap and the decisions needed; do not treat the absence as implementation freedom.
2. Identify shared interactions affected by this change. Consider navigation/activation, focus return, validation/recovery, visibility/scrolling and mobile keyboard behavior where relevant. Select by impact rather than filling an exhaustive catalog.
3. Record expected behavior across affected controls and contexts, including exceptions and conflicts. Reuse the application policy by link. Keep a proposed decision separate from accepted requirements; name what a human still needs to decide.

The implementation handoff must include these inputs even when its allowed reading set is deliberately small. A fresh-context experiment that omits them tests an incomplete contract; preserve that limitation rather than silently importing historical knowledge.

## Before handing off for review

Use a small coverage table in the existing application record or verification notes:

| Requirement / decision source | Affected path and expected result | Evidence and execution conditions | Result / remaining gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Link to shared policy, including candidate status | Concrete start, action, destination/state; relevant counterpart or exception | Exact implementation revision, test or browser/device run | Passed within stated scope, failed, unverified, or not applicable with reason |

Cover transitions across component boundaries, not just each component separately. For focus changes, include forward and reverse traversal through neighboring controls, both equivalent fields, conditional/hidden actions, and the path after a popup closes or invalid input recovers when affected. Include one discriminating operation-order change when prior state may affect the result. Use desktop and mobile contexts where their interaction differs; do not assume a narrow viewport reproduces a software keyboard.

Automate deterministic regressions when useful. Use actual browser operation for claims about native focus traversal, visibility, or event delivery; handler fixtures and screenshots alone do not establish those claims. When execution is unavailable, record the blocked condition and the exact pending path. A review candidate may still be delivered, but application interaction verification remains incomplete. Human design approval remains separate from all verification.

When a shared policy changes, identify affected consumers and evidence that must be revisited. Do not silently retain approval or stale passing results. No fixed test framework, all-screen retest, or new orchestration is required: select checks by the affected responsibility and risk.

## Why this check exists

PoC 018 exposed a handoff gap: the Foundation named application consistency, but the implementation entry point asked only for a bounded Reference. Enter behavior was then corrected locally more than once, and component checks did not establish browser-level navigation across the composed form. The owner's request makes application-level applicability and coverage explicit at both entry and handoff.

The corrective controls are the required AGENTS entry, the curation/workflow links, and the PR applicability/evidence section. They expose an omission for review; a filled table is not proof of usability and cannot guarantee that no defect escapes. [Issue #9](https://github.com/mk3008/torrone/issues/9) separately evaluates the value of AI browser review; this policy neither assumes its result nor selects its tooling.

The [PoC 018 application record](poc/experiments/018-curated-reference-handoff/application-interaction.md) applies this check retrospectively. Its current Enter choice is still a candidate, not a Torrone-wide convention or a human-approved design.

## Shared text-entry visibility

The following guidance applies to browser-based executable References. Native applications choose their platform controls and verify visibility and focus in their own environment; browser event/scroll mechanics are not a Native implementation contract.

Use ordinary browser text-entry behavior. Do not add application scrolling on editor focus, field switching or keyboard viewport changes as a default Reference requirement. Preserve manual scrolling, reachable editors and focus. Calendar disclosure may reveal its owning input and calendar context; this is a separate responsibility.

The attempted generic keyboard-following correction was withdrawn by the owner on 2026-09-16 after repeated unwanted movement. See the [decision, evidence and reopening conditions](decisions/2026-09-16-withdraw-keyboard-scroll.md). This does not reject input visibility as a usability goal or guarantee that native keyboard behavior is identical across hosts. Environment-specific treatment belongs to a bounded consuming-product decision with actual device verification.

Ask one concrete question only when the context leaves multiple plausible interpretations that would change implementation, such as whether a request to keep every tab visible calls for shrinking the tabs beyond the normal policy. Use a borderline example if helpful. Leave pixel thresholds and boundary test values to implementation when the trigger can be observed directly. If the user wants a preview before deciding a material ambiguity, label the assumed trigger as a proposal.

## Show the part the user is deciding on

- Once the use context is clear enough, use an available image or local drawing tool to produce an actual preview. Keep the first preview to the relevant control and the nearby context needed to judge it. Use one strong proposal when there is one meaningful direction. Compare alternatives only when the user has a real choice, and explain what changes and why. If a usable image cannot be produced in the host, state the limitation plainly.
- For material design decisions, check relevant public primary sources, such as platform guidance, design systems, and accessibility standards. Separate requirements, reference patterns, and design judgment. Keep independent decisions separate during review, then check how the resulting states look together.
- Take choices and corrections in ordinary chat. Record the reason with the decision. When the user brings up a new requirement, update the list and handle it at the point where it affects the design. Preserve explicit requirements and use illustrative labels and styling where the user has left those details open.

## Preserve the intent behind the images

- As part of turning the user's request into an image, write down material layout, state, or behavior decisions you supplied to make the request concrete, even if the user did not mention them. State the condition, the chosen relationship, and why you chose it. For example, when showing an overflow button next to the selected item, say which element keeps its needed width, which takes the remaining room, and how that helps the user read the label. Use ordinary prose in the user's language.
- Present these choices with the image as your interpretation or proposal, distinct from the user's stated requirements. Check the rendered image against the note. If the image introduces an additional material choice, either correct the image or explicitly describe that choice as a proposal. Keep these notes through revisions and carry the surviving decisions and reasons into the Markdown. Ask only about choices whose resolution materially changes the design.
- When a design decision is accepted or revised, keep a short working note in the user's language with the condition, the relationship to preserve, and why it matters. Link the decision to the relevant image or conversation when available. Update superseded notes as the discussion changes.
- During image review, call out relationships a still image can leave ambiguous, such as which element grows when room changes, which stays the same, and what happens when another control appears. Explain the consequence for the user. Raise only material unresolved choices, one at a time, and distinguish user-confirmed intent, a proposal that still needs review, and illustrative styling. An image or approval of its appearance alone does not establish the reason or a responsive rule.
- During review, work backward from the image when useful. Ask what you would tell another designer to redraw this state at a different width or with different content while keeping the intended result. Add the few instructions that would affect that result to the working note, along with their reasons. Use an existing generation prompt as evidence when available and describe newly inferred choices as proposals.
- Before saving, compare the accepted discussion, final state images, and draft Markdown. Each relationship that affects implementation must be explained in ordinary prose next to the relevant state or in a nearby shared note. Carry over the condition, what changes or stays stable, and the reason. Fix omissions and contradictions before handoff. If a material intent cannot be verified from the conversation or confirmed requirements, present it as an open question or a clearly labeled proposal.

## Save the agreed draft

After review, save a draft Markdown catalog entry and separate state images in the user's working area or requested destination. Pair each image with a short explanation of the state, what to preserve, and why. Distinguish visual decisions from behavior and accessibility checks that require a working implementation. Preserve existing approvals and ask for human review before treating a new entry as accepted. Report completion after the images and their explanations are saved and the image links work.

# Handoff

## Status

- `done`: standalone static app at `/`, with all fixture cases selected by `?case=`.
- `done`: responsive document/item rows, desktop clipping controls, narrow choosers, close behavior, keyboard tab operation, focus transfer and empty state.
- `not done`: human visual approval and real assistive-technology/device review are outside this browser pass.

## Inputs and design references

- Data: `/bench/fixture.json` (copied into the app logic without changing order or labels).
- Icons: official supplied Lucide SVG files in `/bench/icons`; copied as separate assets, with license.
- Torrone catalog examples actually consulted: `POPOVER-001` for a trailing-edge-aligned anchored item list and `ICON-BUTTON-001` for independent icon-command focus. `TEXT-BUTTON-001` was listed in the catalog but its README was not present, so no behavior was inferred from it.
- The shared brief is the application interaction source. It overrides the catalog's illustrative geometry and styling.

## Browser review and repair

Tools used: static Python server, Playwright with installed Chromium, DOM geometry/accessibility-state assertions, PNG screenshots, and the benchmark image viewer.

First pass:

- At 1180 px, all eight 140 px document tabs correctly fit the 1148 px inner workspace, so no arrows appeared; the initial test expectation was corrected to test overflow at 1000 px.
- At 390 px, screenshots confirmed the selected tab/count composition, exact 6 px surface gap, right-aligned item list, two-column document cards, truncation, and connected tab/content surfaces.
- Found that opening the item chooser left focus on its trigger instead of moving into the chooser.

Repair:

- Moved focus to the first hidden item when its chooser opens.
- Made document chooser entry, chooser dismissal, card selection, item selection, and post-close focus transfers deterministic.

Recheck:

- `node test.cjs`: desktop arrows and selection preservation, narrow chooser/card flow, item selection/focus return, 600 px breakpoint, and focus-without-selection passed.
- `node final-check.cjs`: 12 focused checks passed, including independent row overflow, wheel movement, fit restoration, 6 px narrow gap, both Escape returns, inactive/selected close behavior, selected-item memory, and unknown-case fallback.
- Evidence: `evidence/first-*.png`, `evidence/final-narrow.png`, `evidence/first-report.json`, and `evidence/final-report.json`.

## Run

No build is required. See `README.md`; serve this directory and open the root URL.
EOF
